assertion: Portland's average temperature so far this November is 48 degrees. That ranks as the third-warmest start to November on record.
inaccuracy: Full threaded record: 2022 50.60, 1938 50.17, 1975 48.23 are warmer; 2026 ties 1969 at 48.00, so tied 4th; third only on a post-1941 record. The URL/headline says second-warmest.

assertion: The warmest day so far was November 4, when the temperature reached 73 degrees.
This year, Portland's average high over that same period has been 57 degrees.
The warmest first half of November came in 2022, with an average temperature of 50.6 degrees.
Nearly every day so far this November has been warmer than average in Portland.
inaccuracy: Roughly 9-10 of 15 days were above the ~42 F normal; Nov 1 and Nov 12-15 were at or below normal.

assertion: The city typically receives 4.25 inches over the course of the month. So far, 1.13 inches has fallen, with measurable precipitation recorded on six days.
inaccuracy: 1.13 in is right, but is compared with a full-month normal; the Nov 1-15 normal (1991-2020 mean) is about 2.0 in, so to-date is about 56% of normal, not 27%. Only 5 days had at least 0.01 in; two more were trace.

independent_value: Portland Oct 2026 1.67 in; Maine 2.31 in, 22nd driest since 1895 (drought.gov)

assertion: Severe drought still stretches from York County to Aroostook County. Extreme drought remains across the Midcoast and parts of Aroostook County.
inaccuracy: USDM week of Nov 10: D3 (extreme) covers 82% of Lincoln, 70% Knox, 68% Sagadahoc, 19% Aroostook, 14% Cumberland; D2 present in York (34%) and Aroostook (65%). Many counties are mostly D1-D2, so severe is dominant in places, not uniform.

assertion: The Climate Prediction Center's outlook favors warmer-than-average temperatures through the end of November.
reason: CPC 8-14 day page (valid Nov 24-30, updated Nov 16) loaded but the outlook map is an image; probabilities not readable.
measure: Climate Prediction Center 8-14 day temperature outlook

assertion: A shift in the polar vortex pattern is possible in late November or early December, which could open the door to cooler temperatures.
reason: A hedged forecast of future weather; no evidence can test it today.
